svg.text: The home visit: you are a guest, and the family is the service
What you cannot see in a clinic is the whole point of going
What the visit reveals that a clinic cannot
Whether there is food in the house today
How far the latrine is, and how dark the path
Which medicines are really being taken
Who is actually providing the care, and
whether that person is coping
Whether she is safe with the people she lives with
How to teach a family carer
Use what the household already owns
Demonstrate, then watch her do it herself
One or two things per visit, not a lecture
Write or draw it in a language she reads
Name the signs that mean call us today
A carer who was only told is a carer who was not taught
The carer is a second patient
Exhaustion, no sleep, no income, no relief, and guilt for resenting any of it
Ask her directly how she is sleeping and when she last left the house
A carer who collapses produces an emergency admission for the person she cares for
Signs that should raise concern
Injuries that do not fit the explanation
Left alone all day, unwashed, no water in reach
Her pension collected by someone else
Neglect is the commonest form, and the quietest
Whose home it is
Ask before you move furniture or open
a cupboard. Advice can be refused.
Negotiate what is possible for this family,
not what would be ideal in a ward
